prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right one depends on your budget, health needs, comfort with technology, and whether you want in‑person help or are fine working remotely. I can, however, tell you how to find a top broker in Kansas City, MO and what to look for, and I can pull a short list of well‑rated local brokers if you’d like.

Quick summary — best-broker characteristics for a self‑employed buyer
- Independent broker (represents multiple carriers) so you can compare plans and prices.
- Experienced with the ACA Marketplace (Healthcare.gov) and off‑exchange plans.
- Helps with subsidy eligibility and cost‑sharing reductions if you qualify.
- Provides year‑round service (not just during Open Enrollment) for claims, renewals, and life changes.
- Transparent about fees and commissions (some brokers charge a fee, many are paid by carriers).
- Good local reviews and a clean licensing/complaint history.

How to find and vet brokers in Kansas City, MO
- Use Healthcare.gov “Find Local Help” to locate agents certified to enroll people in Marketplace plans. Missouri uses the federal exchange, so that tool is useful.  
- Search local independent agencies (Google, Yelp) and check BBB ratings and client reviews.  
- Verify licensing and complaints with the Missouri Department of Insurance (they can confirm the agent/broker’s license and any disciplinary actions).  
- Ask these questions when you talk to a broker:
  - Are you independent or captive (do you only sell one carrier’s plans)?
  - Which carriers do you work with locally (BCBS of KC, UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Humana, etc.)?
  - Do you help with Marketplace subsidies and exemptions?
  - Will you assist year‑round with claims and renewals?
  - Do you charge a broker fee? If so, how much and when?
  - Can you show plan comparisons (premiums, deductibles, networks, drug coverage) for multiple options?

Local resources and organizations to use
- Healthcare.gov “Find Local Help” (certified agents and brokers) — for ACA Marketplace help.
- Missouri Department of Insurance — verify licenses and file complaints.
- Local NAHU chapter (National Association of Health Underwriters) — can point to credentialed agents.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and provide a short list (3–5) of top‑rated Kansas City, MO brokers or independent agencies, with phone numbers, websites, and a brief note on whether they handle Marketplace plans and small‑group policies.
Tell me if you’d like an in‑person broker, or whether remote help (phone/email) is fine, and whether you prefer a large agency or a small independent broker. That will let me tailor the list.
